name: Tutorial comments in the game code
body: Dean wants the game code to read like a tutorial: explain what each hook, module and system does, and for every calculation say why it is done and how it gets the gameplay or rendering result.
comments: 2026-10-29: comments added to all 18 .nyx files; code identical after stripping comments; lantern-game-host tests pass. Decision D-042.
plan: Comments only, no behaviour change. Cover every .nyx file in games/platformer/. Lead each file with what it is for and where it sits in the frame (fixed step, display frame, render). For the maths (camera spherical coordinates, yaw/forward/right vectors, turn clamping, cosine easing, sine bob, capsule-vs-sphere touch test, shadow sizing, frame-rate independence, interpolation alpha) explain the formula and the reason. Where a result comes from the engine's character controller (jump speed sqrt(2gh), acceleration, variable jump, coyote time, jump buffer), explain it from the game side and point at crates/physics/src/controller.rs. Record the comment conventions as a decision in docs/decisions.md.
acceptance_criteria: Every .nyx file in games/platformer/ has a header comment saying what it is and how it connects to the engine seam
Every non-trivial calculation has a comment saying what it computes and why
The game-host tests (headless game, course traversal, host surface) pass unchanged
definition_of_done: PR into proto reviewed by Dean
questions: Should the engine-side Rust (controller, frame loop) get the same tutorial treatment later? Out of scope for now; the game comments point at the Rust where it does the maths.
